html:
Bagan, once spelled Pagan, was a city on the Irrawaddy River in central Myanmar and the capital of the Pagan Kingdom, the first state to unite the lands that became Burma. On this map in 1200 it marks that kingdom at its height.

The city was founded in the 9th century by the Bamar people coming south from the hills. In 1044 Anawrahta took the throne and built a kingdom across the Irrawaddy valley. Tradition says he adopted Theravada Buddhism after conquering the Mon city of Thaton. His successor Kyansittha built the Ananda Temple.

In the 11th to 13th centuries Bagan's kings and people built more than 10,000 temples, pagodas and monasteries on the plain around the city; over 2,000 still stand. The kingdom was a rival and partner of the Khmer Empire. It weakened as tax-free temple land grew, and after the Mongol invasions of the late 13th century it broke apart. Bagan is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
